American Mink.png.geography_note: Native North American range retained across Alaska, Canada and most of the contiguous US, but not high-Arctic tundra or introduced Eurasian range. Habitat audit emphasizes riparian/wetland systems within forest, grassland and shrubland landscapes.
American Mink.png.population_note: Normally solitary and territorial, especially adults; temporary breeding pairing only.

European Pine Marten.png.geography_note: Audit tightened: forested Europe from Iberia/British Isles through central, northern and eastern Europe; PA20 removed to avoid overpainting the driest southeastern/Mediterranean fringe.
European Pine Marten.png.population_note: Predominantly solitary and territorial; adults associate chiefly for mating.

European Polecat.png.geography_note: Audit tightened to its established western/central/eastern European native range. PA20 removed as an over-broad southeastern/Mediterranean assignment.
European Polecat.png.population_note: Primarily solitary; temporary breeding pairing is the appropriate managed-zoo abstraction.

Least Weasel.png.geography_note: Audit tightened slightly: very broad Palearctic native range retained, but PA20 removed to avoid blanket coverage of the warmest southeastern/Mediterranean fringe.
Least Weasel.png.population_note: Normally solitary and territorial; temporary breeding pairing only.

Meerkat.png.geography_note: Restricted to arid southwestern southern Africa: chiefly the Kalahari/Karoo system, with western Namibian and extreme southwestern Angolan occurrence. Removed blanket southern-African regions.

Stone Marten.png.geography_note: Widespread from continental Europe and the Mediterranean through the Balkans/Black Sea region into western Asia; PA29 included for its Southwest Asian extension.
Stone Marten.png.population_note: Primarily solitary and territorial; no routine stable social group.

Caracal.png.geography_note: Very broad dry/open-country cat across Africa, Arabia and into Southwest/South Asia. Dense equatorial rainforest is largely avoided; genuine North African and Asian occurrence retained.

Common Genet.png.geography_note: Broad African genet with native southwestern European populations. False African oceanic-island codes removed; mainland African and genuine Iberian/Balearic-range context retained.

Coyote.png.geography_note: Audit removes NA3 North Alaskan Tundra as over-generous. Modern range still spans Alaska/Canada, nearly all contiguous US and Mexico into Central America; broad habitat tolerance retained.
Coyote.png.population_note: Coyotes form durable breeding pairs and commonly live as family units; larger packs are generally extended families rather than wolf-like unrelated packs.

Serval.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan African cat, but absent from true rainforest cores and oceanic islands. Removed Amsterdam/St Paul, Mascarenes, Seychelles/Comoros, St Helena/Ascension and Central/North Congolian rainforest blanket assignments.

Siberian Weasel.png.geography_note: Audit removes IM5–IM7 as too coarse/over-generous. Native range is Palearctic Asia from west of the Urals across Siberia to the Far East and south through China/Korea to Taiwan and the Himalayas; represented here with PA regions only.
Siberian Weasel.png.population_note: Generally solitary outside the reproductive period; no evidence for a normal stable group profile.

Yellow Mongoose.png.geography_note: Southern African dry grassland and shrubland mongoose. Existing compact range confirmed.

African Civet.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan African civet from Senegal/Mauritania east to the Horn and south to northeastern Namibia, Botswana and South Africa. Introduced São Tomé occurrence excluded; no Arabian range.

African Wild Dog.png.geography_note: Current resident-range emphasis: fragmented populations concentrated in southern and East Africa, with small Central/West African remnants. Dense Congo rainforest excluded; historical range is not used to fill former occupancy.

Bat-Eared Fox.png.geography_note: Disjunct arid/semi-arid range: eastern population from southern Sudan/Ethiopia/Somalia through Kenya to SW Tanzania, and southern population from Angola/Namibia/Botswana to Mozambique/South Africa. Removed blanket Sub-Saharan region set.

Cheetah.png.geography_note: Fragmented African open-country distribution plus surviving Iranian population context; AT2/AT16 removed from overly broad shared African array.

European Mink.png.geography_note: Final audit: current native range only, represented conservatively as three separated OneEarth-region remnants corresponding to SW France/northern Spain and the Danube/eastern-European refugia. Historical European range is intentionally excluded. Habitat tags emphasize riparian and wetland dependence.
European Mink.png.population_note: Semi-aquatic mustelid that is normally solitary outside breeding; no stable pair/group profile.

Jungle Cat.png.geography_note: Wetland/grassland cat from northeastern Africa and the Middle East through South and Southeast Asia. African oceanic-island or sub-Saharan blanket assignments excluded.

Spotted Hyena.png.geography_note: Current patchy sub-Saharan distribution, especially fragmented in West/Central Africa but still broad across East and southern Africa. North African historical range excluded.

Stoat.png.geography_note: Broad native Holarctic Eurasian distribution retained. European and northern Eurasian coverage is appropriate; no Mediterranean expansion added.
Stoat.png.population_note: Solitary territorial mustelid outside reproductive encounters.

African Lion.png.geography_note: Current fragmented sub-Saharan lion range in savanna, grassland and shrubland. Broad open-country distribution retained; dense rainforest systems are not treated as continuous range.

Asiatic Black Bear.png.geography_note: Audit trims the previous blanket Indomalayan assignment. Native range is patchy from SE Iran/Pakistan through the Himalayas, China and mainland Southeast Asia, plus Russian Far East/Koreas, Taiwan and Japan. IM13/16/17 removed to avoid overpainting areas beyond the documented mainland range; Malaysia remains excluded.
Asiatic Black Bear.png.population_note: Primarily solitary outside mating and mother-young associations; retain solitary with temporary breeding pairing.

Black-Backed Jackal.png.geography_note: Two major eastern and southern African population systems in open and dry habitats. Existing range retained; similarity to Kori Bustard is biologically plausible.
Black-Backed Jackal.png.population_note: Core social unit is a monogamous breeding pair with dependent or retained young; family helpers can remain with the parents.

Egyptian Mongoose.png.geography_note: Broad African species with native North African and southwestern European populations; African range is patchy around humid forest interiors and extreme deserts. Genuine Iberian range retained.

Gray Fox.png.geography_note: Broad southern North American to Central American/northern South American range retained. Habitat audit emphasizes wooded/brushy landscapes; open northern plains and high-Arctic/boreal interiors remain excluded.
Gray Fox.png.population_note: Usually organized around a breeding pair and offspring; not treated as a stable large-pack canid.

Honey Badger.png.geography_note: Very broad African-to-South Asian species. False Afrotropical oceanic-island codes AT1/AT18 removed while genuine North African, Arabian and South Asian range is retained.

Narrow-Striped Boky.png.geography_note: Final audit confirms AT6 only. Endemic to western Madagascar, especially the dry deciduous forests of central and southern Menabe; no separate mainland-African region is appropriate.
Narrow-Striped Boky.png.population_note: Field studies show stable female units of 1–3 adult females plus offspring and separate male associations of 2–4 adults; therefore generic pair-only treatment is inappropriate.

Sable.png.geography_note: Audit tightened to the native forest belt from the Urals across Siberia and the Russian Far East, with extensions into Mongolia, China, North Korea and Hokkaido. PA2 removed as overly Arctic; no range south into the broader East Asian/Indomalayan belt.
Sable.png.population_note: Solitary and territorial for most of the year; space 2 retained because it is a larger, highly active arboreal/terrestrial marten.

Slender Mongoose.png.geography_note: One of Africa's most widespread mongooses, from Senegal to the Red Sea and south to South Africa. Zanzibar occurrence is native/current; erroneous Cape Verde records do not expand wild_regions.
Slender Mongoose.png.population_note: Generally solitary/small-unit mongoose; provisional profile retained pending zoo-specific husbandry evidence.

Swift Fox.png.geography_note: Audit tightened to the Northern Prairie (NA12) and Southern Prairie Mixed Grasslands (NA20). NA21 Midwestern Tallgrass Prairie & Forest Transition removed because the species' modern/core distribution is the drier shortgrass/mixed-grass Great Plains farther west.
Swift Fox.png.population_note: Generally monogamous, with the breeding pair and pups forming the normal social unit; retained daughters may occasionally help rear a later litter.

Aardwolf.png.geography_note: Disjunct eastern and southern African open-country distribution. Existing broad array confirmed as appropriate.

Blanford's Fox.png.geography_note: Final audit retains the conservative PA29–35 treatment for its discontinuous Sinai/Arabian/Iranian-Central Asian rocky-desert range. No Ethiopian/Horn AT region is used.
Blanford's Fox.png.population_note: Pair/family-unit treatment retained; small body size and rocky-arid ecology fit space level 1 despite its high rarity level.

Ethiopian Wolf.png.geography_note: Final audit confirms AT21 only. Ethiopian Wolf is restricted to isolated Afroalpine highlands of Ethiopia (including Bale, Arsi, Simien and northern highland populations), so no broader East African AT regions are justified.
Ethiopian Wolf.png.population_note: Highly social canid living in territorial packs, commonly 3–13 individuals; pack/breeding-group treatment is more appropriate than pair-based profiles.

Grandidier's Vontsira.png.geography_note: Final audit confirms AT6 only. Extremely restricted endemic of southwestern Madagascar's spiny/dry vegetation mosaic; Madagascar Island remains the appropriate OneEarth region.
Grandidier's Vontsira.png.population_note: Best-supported zoo abstraction is a stable adult pair, sometimes accompanied by offspring. Evidence is limited and some field work suggests more complex/possibly less pair-bonded spatial organisation, so no larger routine group profile is added.
Grandidier's Vontsira.png.taxonomy_note: Retained as a species for Zoo Curator. IUCN and Zootierliste recognize Galidictis grandidieri as a species; ITIS currently treats it as Galidictis fasciata grandidieri. Do not create a separate subspecies card if taxonomy changes.
Grandidier's Vontsira.png.rarity_note: Zootierliste current holdings: 1 European non-EU holder (Chester); level 5 retained.

Marsh Mongoose.png.geography_note: Wetland-associated mainland African species from Senegal through Congo/East Africa to southern Africa. Oceanic islands and driest Kalahari/Horn-coastal blanket regions removed.
Marsh Mongoose.png.population_note: Primarily solitary; pair allowance retained for managed breeding rather than representing a naturally stable large group.

Side-Striped Jackal.png.geography_note: Central/eastern African woodland-savanna species extending into parts of West and southern Africa; removed oceanic islands and arid southwest/Horn-coastal overreach.
Side-Striped Jackal.png.population_note: Usually solitary or paired while foraging, but monogamous pairs and their offspring form the normal family unit; occasional larger aggregations are not treated as a routine profile.

White-Tailed Mongoose.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan mongoose from West Africa to the Horn and southeast South Africa, with genuine Arabian Peninsula populations from Saudi Arabia/Yemen through Oman/UAE. Arabian range added rather than treating it as an African-Civet clone.
White-Tailed Mongoose.png.population_note: Predominantly solitary; pair allowance retained for managed breeding.

Domestic Donkey.png.geography_note: Domestic animal derived from African wild ass; wild_regions intentionally empty because the card represents the domestic donkey rather than a wild taxon.

Pot-Bellied Pig.png.geography_note: Domestic Vietnamese pig breed associated with northern Vietnam/Red River Delta; no wild bioregion distribution assigned.

Shetland Pony.png.geography_note: Domestic breed originating in the Shetland Islands, Scotland; no wild bioregion distribution assigned.

Lechwe.png.geography_note: Wetland antelope of south-central African floodplains, chiefly the Okavango/Upper Zambezi, Kafue and Bangweulu systems. False AT18 oceanic-island assignment and West African displacement removed.

Plains Zebra.png.geography_note: Open grassland/savanna zebra from East Africa south through Zambia/Zimbabwe/Botswana/Namibia to South Africa. False oceanic-island code AT18 and West/Central forest overreach removed.

Red River Hog.png.geography_note: West and Central African forest species from Upper Guinea through the Congo basin, extending locally toward the Great Lakes. Old shared forest-template range included inappropriate East/southern African regions.

Addax.png.geography_note: Sahara/Sahel desert antelope; retained Southern Sahara and Sahel bioregions rather than blanket sub-Saharan Africa.

Blesbok.png.geography_note: Native Highveld grasslands of South Africa; modern extra-limital ranch populations excluded.

Blue Wildebeest.png.geography_note: Eastern and southern African savannas/woodlands; West African, Sahel, Congo forest and island regions removed.

Bongo.png.geography_note: Disjunct forest antelope range: western/central African lowland forests plus isolated montane populations in Kenya and adjacent East African highlands. Shared template replaced with a range reflecting both western and eastern populations.

Common Eland.png.geography_note: Broad savanna and woodland species across eastern and southern Africa with historical/current western Sahel-Sudanian occurrence; Congo rainforest and coastal forests excluded.

Common Warthog.png.geography_note: Broad open-country distribution confirmed: northern savanna/Sahel from Mauritania to Ethiopia, Horn populations, East/Central Africa, and southern Africa.

Common Waterbuck.png.geography_note: Mainland sub-Saharan water-associated antelope from central/eastern Africa into south-central and southeastern Africa. False AT18 island assignment and West African/oceanic blanket regions removed.

Impala.png.geography_note: Eastern and southern African savannas and woodlands; removed Congo rainforest, West Africa and Sahel blanket assignments.

Pygmy Hippopotamus.png.geography_note: Current native range is restricted to the Upper Guinean forest zone of Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire. Extinct Nigerian population excluded.

Sitatunga.png.geography_note: Disjunct swamp/wet-forest antelope: small West African populations plus major Congo Basin, Great Lakes, Zambezi/Okavango systems. Dry southern AT8/AT10 removed.

Springbok.png.geography_note: Southwestern/southern African arid and open-country antelope. Existing range confirmed; equality with Yellow Mongoose is ecologically plausible rather than treated as corruption.

Asian Elephant.png.geography_note: Existing game geography retained unchanged when moved from Other Mammals to Ungulates.

Black Sable Antelope.png.geography_note: Southern/east-central African sable-antelope range centered on Angola/Zambia/DRC-Tanzania south through Malawi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and northern South Africa. False AT18 oceanic-island assignment removed.

Black Wildebeest.png.geography_note: Native open grasslands of the South African Highveld/Karoo transition; extra-limital introductions excluded.

Cape Buffalo.png.geography_note: African buffalo species-level range across suitable sub-Saharan savanna, woodland and forest mosaics. False AT18 island assignment removed; broad mainland range retained.

Chinese Goral.png.geography_note: Native to eastern/central Asia; Chinese goral range centred on China and adjacent mainland East/Southeast Asia. wild_regions use the game's OneEarth PA codes.

Gemsbok.png.geography_note: Arid southwestern Africa centered on Namibia, Botswana and the Kalahari, with northern South African/Angolan margins; unrelated eastern/western regions removed.

Greater Kudu.png.geography_note: Broad eastern and southern African woodland/bushland range; retained genuine Horn/Great Lakes margins but excluded West Africa, Congo rainforest and islands.

Hippopotamus.png.geography_note: Current fragmented mainland sub-Saharan freshwater range. False oceanic-island codes AT3/AT4/AT5/AT18 removed; Madagascar excluded.

Kordofan Giraffe.png.geography_note: Current Kordofan giraffe range: southern Chad, northern Central African Republic, northern Cameroon, northwestern DRC and western South Sudan. Removed impossible island/coastal/equatorial blanket assignments; retained every OneEarth bioregion genuinely intersecting that fragmented range.

Nyala.png.geography_note: Southeastern African thicket/woodland distribution from Malawi/Mozambique/Zimbabwe into eastern South Africa; unrelated western/northern regions removed.

Red Buffalo.png.geography_note: Forest buffalo distribution centered on West and Central African rainforest systems, extending into the Congo basin. Old East/southern African savanna-style array removed.

Red Duiker.png.geography_note: Southeastern African forest/thicket duiker from southern Tanzania through Malawi and Mozambique to eastern Zimbabwe, Eswatini and eastern South Africa. False AT18 island and West/Central overreach removed.

Reticulated Giraffe.png.geography_note: Current native range is concentrated in northern/northeastern Kenya with small populations in southern Ethiopia and southern Somalia. Limited to the Lake Turkana-Sudd/Horn and South Red Sea-Gulf of Aden dryland systems; Congo and southern-African regions removed.

Rothschild's Giraffe.png.geography_note: Rothschild's/Nubian giraffe populations represented by their native East African range in Uganda and western Kenya. Greater subequatorial savanna, Victoria-Albertine and northern East African grassland systems retained; Central Congo removed.

White Rhinoceros.png.geography_note: Current/native southern African white-rhinoceros range centered on South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe and historically adjacent south-central savannas; old Central/West African and AT18 island assignments removed.

African Elephant.png.geography_note: Existing game geography retained unchanged when moved from Other Mammals to Ungulates.

Angolan Giraffe.png.geography_note: Angolan giraffe is a southwestern African form, centered on Namibia with range into Angola and Botswana. Corrected a severely displaced former array that included St Helena, West Africa, Sudan and East Africa.

Black Rhinoceros.png.geography_note: Current fragmented eastern and southern African range. West/Central African and false AT18 oceanic-island assignments removed; extinct historical range does not expand wild_regions.

Blue Duiker.png.geography_note: Forest-associated species from West/Central Africa through East African coastal/highland forests to southeastern Africa and the eastern/southern Cape. False AT18 island assignment and dry Sahel/Horn blanket regions removed.

Cuvier's Gazelle.png.geography_note: Northwest African mountain and steppe gazelle of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. Sub-Saharan and oceanic-island assignments excluded.

Gerenuk.png.geography_note: Horn of Africa and dry bushlands of northern/eastern Kenya and adjacent Ethiopia/Somalia; removed unrelated sub-Saharan regions.

Klipspringer.png.geography_note: Patchily distributed rocky-country antelope from the Horn/Ethiopian highlands through East Africa to southern Africa and southwest Angola/Namibia. Forest-belt regions inherited from the old broad template removed.

Masai Giraffe.png.geography_note: East African giraffe centered on Kenya and Tanzania with adjacent populations; range distinguished from southeastern African forest taxa.

Mountain Reedbuck.png.geography_note: Discontinuous montane grassland populations in Ethiopia/East Africa and southeastern/southern Africa. Sahel, Congo forest, southwest desert and false AT18 island assignments removed.

Saiga.png.geography_note: Native steppe and semi-desert of Central Asia; principally Kazakhstan, with populations/range extending into adjacent parts of Russia, Mongolia and Uzbekistan. wild_regions use the game's OneEarth PA codes.

Yellow-Backed Duiker.png.geography_note: Broad West/Central African forest and dense-vegetation species extending east to western Uganda/Kenya and south into Zambia/northern Angola. Range separated from the narrower White-Crested Turaco template.

Barbary Macaque.png.geography_note: Current native range is restricted to fragmented populations in Morocco and Algeria (Rif, Middle/High Atlas and Tellian Atlas). Gibraltar is introduced and excluded.

De Brazza's Monkey.png.geography_note: Riverine/swamp forest monkey from Cameroon/CAR through the Congo basin to Uganda, western Kenya, South Sudan and southwestern Ethiopia; rebuilt from its documented west-to-east range.

Green Monkey.png.geography_note: West African green monkey: Atlantic West Africa and adjoining Sudanian/Sahel savannas from Senegal/Gambia eastward. Caribbean/Cape Verde introductions excluded.

Collared Mangabey.png.geography_note: Narrow Atlantic coastal-forest distribution from western Nigeria through southern Cameroon, mainland Equatorial Guinea and Gabon to the Gabon-Congo border; removed unrelated inland/eastern African regions.

Diana Monkey.png.geography_note: Upper Guinean forest endemic from Sierra Leone and Liberia into western Côte d'Ivoire; removed Indian Ocean islands and East/Southern African codes.

Gelada Baboon.png.geography_note: Ethiopian Highlands endemic; restricted to the Horn/highland bioregion rather than southern African savannas.

Mandrill.png.geography_note: West-central African rainforest species south of the Sanaga River, from southern Cameroon through mainland Equatorial Guinea and Gabon into Congo.

Mantled Guereza.png.geography_note: Species-level Colobus guereza range spans Nigeria/Cameroon east across the northern Congo basin to South Sudan/Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya and northern Tanzania. Retains genuine gallery-forest penetration into savanna systems.

Patas Monkey.png.geography_note: Sahelian/Sudanian open-country primate ranging in a broad band south of the Sahara from Senegal east to South Sudan/Ethiopia and south locally to Kenya.

Senegal Bushbaby.png.geography_note: Dry woodland/savanna galago distributed from Senegal across the Sahel to Eritrea/Ethiopia/Somalia and south around the Lake Victoria region; old West-African-only shared template expanded eastward.

Black Crested Mangabey.png.geography_note: Central African species south of the Congo River in DRC/Angola forest systems; removed northern Congo and Gulf-of-Guinea overreach.

Chimpanzee.png.geography_note: Species-level chimpanzee range from Upper Guinea through Gulf of Guinea and Congo forests east to Uganda/Tanzania, with savanna-forest mosaics at northern/western margins. Southern African and oceanic-island regions excluded.

Drill.png.geography_note: Restricted Cross-Sanaga forest species of southeastern Nigeria, western/southwestern Cameroon and Bioko; represented by the Gulf of Guinea coastal-forest bioregion.

Mohol Bushbaby.png.geography_note: Southern lesser galago is a southern African savanna/woodland species from Angola/Namibia/Botswana through Zambia/Zimbabwe and southern DRC toward Mozambique and South Africa; northern Sahel/Horn/West African regions excluded.

Owl-Faced Monkey.png.geography_note: Albertine Rift/eastern Congo montane-forest monkey; restricted to the Albertine and adjacent North Congolian systems.

Vervet Monkey.png.geography_note: Widespread eastern and southern African monkey following savanna, woodland and riverine habitats; central south-tropical reach distinguishes it from Aardwolf.

Western Lowland Gorilla.png.geography_note: West-central African lowland forest range retained across North Congolian and Gulf-of-Guinea forest systems.

Bonobo.png.geography_note: Endemic to DRC forests south of the Congo River; corrected from northern/Gulf-of-Guinea codes to Central and South Congolian systems.

Eastern Gorilla.png.geography_note: Eastern DRC/Uganda/Rwanda montane and lowland populations centered on the Albertine Rift and eastern North Congolian forests.

African Crested Porcupine.png.geography_note: Hystrix cristata spans North Africa plus a broad West-to-East African belt; North-African/Palearctic component restored. European Italian occurrence is not used here to inflate native African-themed geography.

Red-Necked Wallaby.png.geography_note: Native to eastern and southeastern Australia including Tasmania; introduced populations outside Australia excluded.

Sugar Glider.png.geography_note: Using Petaurus breviceps sensu current split: southeastern/eastern Australian population; former broad northern populations assigned to other Petaurus taxa are excluded.

Cape Porcupine.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan porcupine in most vegetated habitats, absent from the southwestern coastal desert. Broad range is legitimate and differs from the rocky, patchy Klipspringer distribution.

Egyptian Fruit Bat.png.geography_note: Cave-roosting fruit bat with a discontinuous range across much of sub-Saharan Africa plus the Nile/North Africa, eastern Mediterranean and Middle East. Old all-purpose wetland/reptile-style African array refined.

Long-Eared Hedgehog.png.geography_note: Dry-country hedgehog from the eastern Mediterranean/Middle East through Central and South Asia. No sub-Saharan or Afrotropical-island range.

Red Kangaroo.png.geography_note: Arid and semi-arid mainland Australia; removed Queensland rainforest and all Australasian-island/Pacific regions.

Round-Eared Elephant Shrew.png.geography_note: Macroscelides proboscideus sensu current split is the Karoo round-eared sengi of South Africa, southern Namibia and extreme southwestern Botswana; restricted to Cape/Karoo/Namib-adjacent drylands.

Swamp Wallaby.png.geography_note: Eastern and southeastern mainland Australia only; removed western/interior regions outside the native range.

Agile Wallaby.png.geography_note: Northern tropical Australia plus southern New Guinea; corrected erroneous New Zealand/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate/Indomalayan assignments.

Black-and-Rufous Elephant Shrew.png.geography_note: Rhynchocyon petersi is an East African coastal/lowland and montane forest species of Kenya and Tanzania, including Zanzibar; Congo-basin blanket regions removed.

Brushtail Possum.png.geography_note: Native across Australia including Tasmania. New Zealand is introduced and excluded; Pacific, New Guinea, Sulawesi and subantarctic regions removed.

Eastern Wallaroo.png.geography_note: Eastern wallaroo/euro range across eastern and inland mainland Australia; all offshore Australasian island regions removed.

Grey Kangaroo.png.geography_note: Macropus giganteus is the Eastern Grey Kangaroo: eastern and southeastern Australia including Tasmania; western Australia and offshore island bioregions removed.

Long-Nosed Potoroo.png.geography_note: Coastal and subcoastal southeastern Australia including Tasmania; removed western, interior and subantarctic regions.

Rodriguez Flying Fox.png.geography_note: Endemic to Rodrigues Island (Mauritius), not Madagascar itself; AT6 removed.

Western Woylie.png.geography_note: Current/native southwestern and southern Australian range; corrected erroneous northern-Australia and Pacific-island codes.

Aardvark.png.geography_note: Genuinely widespread mainland sub-Saharan species, but not an oceanic-island animal and generally absent from the wettest Congo rainforest core. Broad range retained where suitable savanna, woodland, grassland and dryland habitat occurs.

African Brush-Tailed Porcupine.png.geography_note: Forest and forest-mosaic porcupine from Upper Guinea through Gulf of Guinea and Congo forests east to Uganda/Kenya/South Sudan; broad dry southern-African regions removed.

Common Wombat.png.geography_note: Southeastern Australia and Tasmania; removed interior/western Australia and all Australasian island spillover.

Dusky Pademelon.png.geography_note: Native to southern New Guinea and the Aru Islands, all within OneEarth New Guinea & Surrounding Islands (AU13). Corrected erroneous IM18 Sumatra/Malaysia assignment.

Koala.png.geography_note: Native eastern Australia from Queensland through New South Wales/Victoria into South Australia; removed New Guinea, Solomon, Sulawesi and other island regions.

Rock Hyrax.png.geography_note: Rocky-country mammal with discontinuous African and Arabian/Levant populations; broad open-country template narrowed away from unrelated wetland/flamingo geography.

Short-Beaked Echidna.png.geography_note: Native throughout Australia including Tasmania and in southern/eastern New Guinea; introduced/irrelevant NZ, Pacific, Sulawesi and Indomalayan codes removed.

Yellow-Footed Rock Wallaby.png.geography_note: Restricted to rocky ranges of South Australia, New South Wales and southwestern Queensland; removed tropical/Pacific/New Guinea regions.

Platypus.png.geography_note: Eastern Australian freshwater systems and Tasmania; removed western/interior Australia and all offshore Australasian island spillover.

Tasmanian Devil.png.geography_note: Wild native population is Tasmania; AU16 is the Subantarctic Antipodes Islands and was erroneous.

White-Striped Dorcopsis.png.geography_note: Endemic to northern New Guinea; corrected erroneous AU1 New Zealand assignment.

Black Kite.png.geography_note: Black Kite sensu Milvus migrans: broad Eurasian breeding/resident range, with western Palearctic migrants wintering chiefly in the Sahel and sub-Saharan Africa. Resident African Yellow-Billed Kite is handled separately as Milvus aegyptius, so its blanket African range is not duplicated here.

Little Owl.png.geography_note: Palearctic owl from Europe and North Africa east through the Middle East and Central Asia. False Afrotropical oceanic-island codes removed; North African occurrence retained.

Western Barn Owl.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Scientific name Tyto alba is Western Barn Owl under the modern split; New World barn owls are American Barn Owl Tyto furcata.
Western Barn Owl.png.geography_note: Pass-42 regression corrected: broad African range retained and the genuine western Palearctic/European–North African range restored. Madagascar retained where represented by the broad Western Barn Owl card concept.

Eurasian Goshawk.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Scientific name Accipiter gentilis is Eurasian Goshawk under the modern split; North American populations are American Goshawk Accipiter atricapillus, a separate species.

Hooded Vulture.png.geography_note: Broad sub-Saharan vulture, strongest in West and East Africa with sparse range-edge populations in southern Africa; oceanic islands and dense Congo rainforest core excluded.

Lanner Falcon.png.geography_note: Broad African and southern Palearctic falcon range retained; its wide African coverage is genuine.

Long-Eared Owl.png.geography_note: Primarily Holarctic owl with North African populations/winter occurrence. False AT1 oceanic-island assignment removed; broad Palearctic range retained.

Peregrine Falcon.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Southern Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego use is not strong enough here to assign the broad NT2 polygon under the conservative seasonal-living rule.

Spotted Eagle-Owl.png.geography_note: Primarily eastern and southern African open-country owl with southwestern and Horn extensions; central/western rainforest and oceanic-island blanket assignments removed.

Steller's Sea Eagle.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Native breeding/resident range is northeastern Asia; Alaska/North American records are vagrancy/exceptional occurrence and do not meet the project's true-living-range rule.

Striated Caracara.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: far-southern Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego/Falklands are the species core.

Turkey Vulture.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Regular South American range reaches Patagonia, but the far-southern NT2 polygon was too broad under the conservative bioregion rule.

African Fish Eagle.png.geography_note: Widespread mainland sub-Saharan eagle tied to lakes, rivers and wetlands from West/Central Africa through East Africa to southern Africa. Oceanic islands and driest interior regions excluded.

African Wood Owl.png.geography_note: Very widespread woodland/forest owl from Senegambia through the Congo Basin and Ethiopia/East Africa to southern Africa. Previous Sitatunga-identical wetland footprint was too narrow.

Andean Condor.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: core resident range genuinely extends through Patagonian Andes to Tierra del Fuego.

Bateleur.png.geography_note: Extensive but increasingly fragmented sub-Saharan savanna/woodland range from southern Mauritania/Senegal across the Sahel and East Africa to Namibia, Botswana and northeastern South Africa; southwest Arabian occurrence represented separately.

Bearded Vulture.png.geography_note: Mountain specialist with fragmented populations in North Africa, East African highlands and the Palearctic/Himalayan belt. Oceanic-island code AT1 and lowland African blanket regions removed.

Ferruginous Pygmy Owl.png.geography_note: Resident widespread Neotropical owl; mapping includes Sonoran/Texan drylands, Central America, seasonally flooded western Amazon, Chaco/Cerrado and Atlantic Forest habitats; dense unflooded Amazon forest is not treated as universal habitat.

Greyish Eagle-Owl.png.geography_note: Northern sub-Saharan species of the Sahel/Sudanian belt and Horn/East African dry country; removed oceanic islands and southern/central African overreach.

Long-Legged Buzzard.png.geography_note: Open dry-country buzzard centered on North Africa, southeastern Europe, the Middle East and Central/South Asia, with regular Sahel/Horn occurrence. Oceanic-island and tropical central/southern African overreach removed.

Palm-Nut Vulture.png.geography_note: West/Central African moist-forest and palm-associated raptor extending east to South Sudan/Kenyan coast and south through Angola to northeastern coastal South Africa. Broad western range restored.

Rüppell's Vulture.png.geography_note: Sahelian and East African vulture: Senegal/Gambia/Mali east to Sudan/South Sudan/Ethiopia, then south through Kenya/Tanzania to Mozambique. Southern-African migrant footprint of Abdim's Stork removed.

Secretary Bird.png.geography_note: Sub-Saharan open-grassland and savanna raptor; North African AT2 and central forest-oriented AT16 removed from inherited broad template.

Short-Eared Owl.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: Short-eared Owl has genuine open-country populations in Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego and island populations, so southern IDs remain defensible.

Tawny Eagle.png.geography_note: Open-country eagle across sub-Saharan Africa with additional South Asian population; North-African/central-forest template regions removed.

Verreaux's Eagle-Owl.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan owl outside deep rainforest, with strongest occurrence in eastern and southern Africa and patchier West African populations.

White-Backed Vulture.png.geography_note: Very widespread sub-Saharan vulture from Senegal/Gambia/Mali through the Sahel and Horn to southern Africa, but generally absent from heavily forested equatorial interiors.

American Barn Owl.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: American Barn Owl reaches far southern South America, but NT2 as a whole overstates established habitat; retain more defensible adjacent/open-country regions.

Barbary Falcon.png.geography_note: Barbary Falcon concept retained for the North African/Middle Eastern peregrine form: Canary/North African desert and mountain systems east through Egypt, the Red Sea/Horn fringe and Arabia/Levant. Oceanic Afrotropical island codes removed.

Bonelli's Eagle.png.geography_note: Primarily Mediterranean-to-Indomalayan rocky-country eagle. In Africa its established breeding range is North African, reaching the northern Sahara fringe; sub-Saharan occurrences are dispersal/vagrancy and do not expand the regular wild_regions.

Brahminy Kite.png.geography_note: Widespread coastal/wetland raptor from the Indian subcontinent through Southeast Asia, Indonesia and New Guinea to northern/eastern Australia and the Bismarck/Solomon region. Broad cross-realm range is genuine.

Martial Eagle.png.geography_note: Very widespread but patchy sub-Saharan raptor from West Africa through East Africa to southern Africa. Added legitimate western occurrence while retaining broad savanna/woodland range.

Short-Toed Snake Eagle.png.geography_note: Breeds from northwestern Africa and southern Europe east through the Levant/Central Asia, with western populations wintering across the Sahel to Ethiopia and western Kenya. Previous oceanic-island and southern-African blanket codes removed.

Verreaux's Eagle.png.geography_note: Patchy rocky/mountainous African range from Eritrea/Ethiopia south through East and southern Africa, with isolated Sahel/Saharan massifs and marginal Arabian occurrence; forest and island codes excluded.

White-Headed Vulture.png.geography_note: Patchily widespread sub-Saharan vulture from Senegambia east to Eritrea/Ethiopia/Somalia and south to South Africa, generally outside forested regions.

Yellow-Billed Kite.png.geography_note: Occurs virtually throughout sub-Saharan Africa and is native on Madagascar and the Comoros, extending north along coastal East Africa to Egypt and into southwestern Arabia. AT6 retained deliberately for Madagascar; unrelated oceanic-island codes removed.

White-Bellied Sea Eagle.png.geography_note: Coastal and large-waterway species from India/Sri Lanka through Southeast Asia and Indonesia to New Guinea and Australia including Tasmania. Broad Indo-Australasian range is genuine; unrelated Pacific/NZ regions excluded.

African Spurred Tortoise.png.geography_note: Sahelian and southern-Sahara tortoise from West Africa east toward Sudan/Eritrea/Ethiopia. Southern-African implication from its former duplicate pairing removed.

Carpet Python.png.geography_note: Australia plus southern New Guinea for the species complex; removed Pacific, Sulawesi and southeast Indonesian spillover.

Central Bearded Dragon.png.geography_note: Arid/semi-arid eastern and central mainland Australia; removed Pacific/New Guinea island regions.

Green Tree Python.png.geography_note: Native to New Guinea and surrounding islands plus Cape York Peninsula, Queensland. Removed erroneous New Zealand assignment and corrected New Guinea to AU13.

Aldabra Giant Tortoise.png.geography_note: Native extant wild range is Aldabra Atoll (Seychelles), not Madagascar itself. A modern rewilding population exists on Madagascar, but it is a managed introduction; AT6 removed.

Dwarf Crocodile.png.geography_note: West and Central African forest-swamp crocodile from the Upper Guinea forests through Lower Guinea and the Congo basin. East/southern African regions from the shared template removed.

Frill-Necked Lizard.png.geography_note: Northern Australia and southern New Guinea; corrected NZ/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate/Indomalayan assignments.

Leopard Tortoise.png.geography_note: Eastern and southern African open-country tortoise, with Horn/East African and southern dryland/grassland coverage; Congo and West African rainforest blanket regions removed.

Pig-Nosed Turtle.png.geography_note: Southern New Guinea and northern Australian river systems; corrected NZ/Lord Howe/Indomalayan assignments.

Red-Bellied Short-Necked Turtle.png.geography_note: New Guinea-region freshwater turtle; corrected erroneous AU1 New Zealand and IM18 Sumatra/Malaysia codes.

Savannah Monitor.png.geography_note: West/Central African savanna monitor, concentrated from Senegal across the Sudanian/Sahel belt into northern Cameroon/CAR and adjacent savanna; rainforest core, East/Southern Africa and oceanic islands removed.

Spiny-Tailed Monitor.png.geography_note: Arid and tropical northern/central/western Australia; removed NZ/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate codes.

African Helmeted Turtle.png.geography_note: Card resolved as Pelomedusa subrufa sensu stricto under modern taxonomy, not the former continent-wide Pelomedusa subrufa complex. Native range represented from southern Angola/Namibia through Botswana and southeastern DRC to Malawi/Tanzania and northeastern South Africa. Madagascar excluded because its population is introduced.

Mediterranean Turtle.png.geography_note: Mediterranean freshwater turtle range in southern Europe, North Africa and adjacent western Asia. False AT1 oceanic-island assignment removed.

Nile Crocodile.png.geography_note: Widespread African freshwater crocodile. Broad African array remains appropriate; PA25 retained for Nile/Sahara-linked range context. Duplicate equality with unrelated taxa is broken by their corrections.

Nile Monitor.png.geography_note: Water-associated monitor across most of sub-Saharan Africa and north along the Nile into Egypt. Oceanic islands and the driest southwest coastal desert removed; Nile-linked North African overlap retained.

Puff Adder.png.geography_note: Very widespread across sub-Saharan Africa outside true rainforest and extreme desert, with an isolated Moroccan population and southwestern Arabian occurrence. Forest-core regions removed; Arabian/North-African edge retained.

Bell's Hinge-Back Tortoise.png.geography_note: Kinixys belliana under the modern narrower species concept: central/eastern Africa from Angola/DRC/Burundi through East Africa and the Horn. Older literature's Senegal-to-South-Africa range included taxa now treated separately; introduced Madagascar records excluded.

Black Mamba.png.geography_note: Open woodland, savanna and rocky-country snake widespread across eastern, central and southern Africa. Sahel-wide AT23 treatment removed; disputed far-western records do not drive the map.

Black-Headed Python.png.geography_note: Northern and central mainland Australia; removed NZ/Lord Howe/southern and Pacific-island spillover.

Central African Rock Python.png.geography_note: Python sebae (Northern/Central African rock python), not the southern Python natalensis: West/Central African and northern East African distribution across savanna, woodland, forest-edge and wetland systems; southern African range excluded.

Eastern Green Mamba.png.geography_note: Coastal and southeastern East African forest/woodland snake from Kenya/Tanzania through Mozambique into northeastern South Africa. Existing compact range confirmed.

Freshwater Crocodile.png.geography_note: Endemic to tropical northern Australia; removed NZ/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate codes.

Green Bush Viper.png.geography_note: Central and East African forest viper associated with Congo-basin and Albertine/eastern forests; old duplicated West/southern savanna-style array removed.

Lace Monitor.png.geography_note: Eastern Australian mainland; removed western/interior and all offshore Australasian island spillover.

Mitchell's Water Monitor.png.geography_note: Restricted to tropical northern Australia; removed NZ/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate/Queensland-rainforest blanket codes.

Saltwater Crocodile.png.geography_note: Established Indo-Pacific range from eastern India/Sri Lanka through Southeast Asia and Indonesia to New Guinea, northern Australia, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. Broad range intentionally retained; New Zealand excluded.

Slender-Snouted Crocodile.png.geography_note: West and Central African river/forest crocodile under the broad card concept; distribution follows Upper Guinean and Congo-basin waters rather than East/southern African savannas.

West African Crocodile.png.geography_note: Crocodylus suchus currently ranges from Mauritania through West/Central Africa as far east as Uganda; Congo/Great-Lakes coverage added while southern/eastern open-country template regions remain excluded.

Perentie.png.geography_note: Arid and semi-arid mainland Australia; removed Lord Howe/eastern-temperate regions.

Tuatara.png.geography_note: Native/relict distribution is New Zealand, chiefly offshore islands and conservation translocations. Corrected OC1 (Easter Island) to AU1 New Zealand.

Amano Shrimp.png.geography_note: Caridina multidentata native to Japan and Taiwan; amphidromous, with freshwater adults and marine larvae. Removed blanket mainland East Asian regions; PA49–52 remain provisional pending exact OneEarth mapping.
Amano Shrimp.png.taxonomy_note: Adults inhabit freshwater streams; amphidromous larvae develop in brackish/marine waters.

Bamboo Shrimp.png.geography_note: Atyopsis moluccensis native to tropical Indo-Pacific mainland/island streams; adults freshwater, larvae marine. Published distribution includes China, Thailand, Malaya, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Philippines. Existing IM codes provisional and need OneEarth-specific review.
Bamboo Shrimp.png.taxonomy_note: Freshwater filter-feeding adults; coastal waters are relevant to larval development, not adult habitat.

Beadlet Anemone.png.geography_note: Actinia equina: rocky intertidal northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean. Usually individual animals rather than true colonies. Existing land-biogeoregion codes are provisional coastal proxies. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Beadlet Anemone.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): intertidal.
Beadlet Anemone.png.marine_mapping_note: Northeastern Atlantic candidate subset, based on overlapping coastal regions used by Small-Spotted Catshark and Grey Seal. Mediterranean portion not yet mapped. Codes are inferred from existing inventory comparators, not independently verified against MEOW polygon boundaries.

Bubble-Tip Anemone.png.geography_note: Entacmaea quadricolor: tropical Indo-Pacific reefs including Red Sea. May be solitary or form dense clonal aggregations; existing land-region codes do not adequately represent Red Sea or ocean provinces. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Bubble-Tip Anemone.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Cherry Shrimp.png.geography_note: Neocaridina davidi native to mainland China and Taiwan; wider Korea/Vietnam nativity is reported but requires region-level verification. Red color is captive-bred. Exclude introductions in Europe, Hawaii and Japan. PA assignments provisional.

Common Crab.png.geography_note: Carcinus maenas is a marine coastal species; current PA codes are land bioregions and should not be interpreted as occupied interiors. Native northeastern Atlantic/Mediterranean only; invasive populations excluded. Marine coast-only distribution: land-based PA codes are provisional, not confirmed species-specific coastal polygons. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.

Common Lobster.png.geography_note: Working identification: European lobster; common name alone is ambiguous. Marine coast-only distribution: land-based PA codes are provisional, not confirmed species-specific coastal polygons. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Common Lobster.png.marine_mapping_note: Provisional northeastern Atlantic candidate subset assuming Homarus gammarus identification; full range not yet mapped. Codes are inferred from existing inventory comparators, not independently verified against MEOW polygon boundaries.

Common Morpho.png.geography_note: Species-level treatment Morpho helenor; Morpho peleides is often treated as M. helenor peleides, a subspecies. Neotropical forest and forest-edge range from Mexico through Central America and South America; existing OneEarth codes remain provisional pending map audit.

Common Prawn.png.geography_note: Working identification: common prawn Palaemon serratus, northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean. Marine coast-only distribution: land-based PA codes are provisional, not confirmed species-specific coastal polygons. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.

Common Starfish.png.geography_note: Asterias rubens: northeastern Atlantic from Arctic Norway to Senegal, with occasional Mediterranean occurrence; some sources also include northwestern Atlantic populations. Current terrestrial PA range is overbroad and provisional pending marine-region mapping. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Common Starfish.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): sandy-seafloor, intertidal.

Curlyhair Tarantula.png.geography_note: Central American terrestrial tarantula; exact national native range is narrower than the broad bioregion approximation.
Curlyhair Tarantula.png.habitat_note: Primarily tropical seasonally dry forest and scrub; rainforest is too broad as a default for this species.

Emperor Scorpion.png.geography_note: West African forest scorpion, sometimes kept in groups with adequate space.
Emperor Scorpion.png.population_note: Can be maintained singly or in carefully managed conspecific groups; group compatibility is conditional, not obligatory.
Emperor Scorpion.png.habitat_note: Humid tropical forest, forest edge and burrows; avoid treating arid dry forest as characteristic.

European Honey Bee.png.geography_note: Apis mellifera is native to Europe, Africa and western Asia, but its present near-global managed/feral distribution is not native range. Existing PA/AT regions are provisional and AT14 (island bioregion) particularly requires reassessment.

Garden Fruit Chafer.png.geography_note: Pachnoda sinuata confirmed by SANBI in South African Western Cape orchard/urban habitats, Beaufort West and Kuruman. AT2/AT8/AT9 are provisional regional approximations; do not interpret as all southern African savannas.

Giant African Land Snail.png.geography_note: East African native range; global invasive/introduced populations excluded.
Giant African Land Snail.png.habitat_note: Often most active in humid evenings and at night, but nocturnality is behavioural rather than an exclusive habitat.

Giant African Millipede.png.geography_note: East and Central African humid forest and woodland litter.

Giant Mealworm Beetle.png.geography_note: Zophobas morio: captive feeder-insect trade is widespread; do not infer a continuous Neotropical wild distribution from commercial availability. Existing broad NT codes require occurrence-level verification.
Giant Mealworm Beetle.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): forest-floor.

Golden-Eyed Stick Insect.png.geography_note: Provisional identification: golden-eyed stick insect; verify exact species against card art.

Leafcutter Ant.png.geography_note: Working identification: Atta cephalotes; common name encompasses many Atta and Acromyrmex species.
Leafcutter Ant.png.population_note: Obligately eusocial colonies with queen and workers; individual ants are not a viable standalone exhibit population.

Long-Spined Sea Urchin.png.geography_note: Provisional identification Diadema antillarum (Caribbean/Western Atlantic). Common name also used for Diadema setosum (Indo-Pacific, including Red Sea). Card illustration must be checked before changing species identity or geography. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Long-Spined Sea Urchin.png.habitat_audit_note: Diadema antillarum occurs on Caribbean and western Atlantic reefs; avoid treating all long-spined urchins worldwide as this species.
Long-Spined Sea Urchin.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Madagascar Hissing Cockroach.png.geography_note: Gromphadorhina portentosa is endemic to Madagascar, especially tropical lowland forest leaf litter. AT6 is a coarse Madagascar regional proxy and needs subregional refinement.
Madagascar Hissing Cockroach.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): forest-floor. Terrestrial forest-floor and decaying-log microhabitats within tropical forest.

Malachite.png.geography_note: Neotropical butterfly from Mexico through Central America and northern South America.

Malayan Jungle Nymph.png.geography_note: Confirmed Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra, Java and Sarawak/Borneo. Excludes unsupported mainland and eastern Indonesian blanket regions; exact OneEarth island-code alignment merits later map check.

Mexican Red Knee Tarantula.png.geography_note: Brachypelma hamorii is restricted to the Pacific slope of western Mexico: Colima, northwestern coastal Michoacán and southern Jalisco. Current NA27/28/29 regional assignments are broad provisional proxies, not evidence of occurrence throughout Mexico. Keep separate from B. smithi.
Mexican Red Knee Tarantula.png.habitat_note: Scientific name Brachypelma hamorii retained; frequently confused with B. smithi in older captive records.

Monarch.png.geography_note: Danaus plexippus: native American populations and long-distance North American migration; Australia (recorded since c.1871) and New Zealand (19th century) are colonized/self-introduced populations, excluded from native-region mapping.

Moon Jelly.png.geography_note: Aurelia aurita sensu stricto: formerly assigned a near-cosmopolitan range, now understood as part of a many-species Aurelia complex. Global records must not be copied to A. aurita. Existing PA/NA region array remains provisional pending taxonomic and marine province mapping. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Moon Jelly.png.taxonomy_audit_note: Aurelia aurita is a valid species, but worldwide moon jellies are a species complex; do not extrapolate global Aurelia observations to A. aurita. Lawley et al. 2021, PeerJ (PMC8435205).
Moon Jelly.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): estuary.

Pacific Sand Dollar.png.geography_note: Dendraster excentricus: northeastern Pacific sandy bottoms from Alaska to Baja California; occurs in dense beds. Terrestrial NA region codes remain provisional and must not imply inland occurrence. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Pacific Sand Dollar.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): sandy-seafloor.

Postman.png.geography_note: Neotropical postman butterfly; common name can also denote Heliconius erato.

Rough Woodlouse.png.geography_note: Native European terrestrial isopod; introduced worldwide.

Scarlet Cleaner Shrimp.png.geography_note: Lysmata amboinensis: Indo-Pacific reef cleaning shrimp including Red Sea and Hawaii; existing terrestrial IM/AU region list omits oceanic range and must be replaced with marine provinces. Do not interpret listed land regions as full native distribution. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Scarlet Cleaner Shrimp.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Spiny Leaf Insect.png.geography_note: Extatosoma tiaratum is native to eastern Australia, principally Queensland and New South Wales. Western Australian records can be introduced. Existing AU3/AU4/AU8/AU9 bioregion codes are unverified and should not be read as an Australia-wide range.
Spiny Leaf Insect.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): woodland.
Spiny Leaf Insect.png.taxonomy_note: Same species as Giant Spiny Stick Insect.png (Extatosoma tiaratum); retain both card filenames until user decides whether to replace one.

Sun Beetle.png.geography_note: Pachnoda marginata is distinct from Garden Fruit Chafer (Pachnoda sinuata); no duplicate. West/Central African savanna and woodland region mapping remains provisional.

Two-Spotted Assassin Bug.png.geography_note: African predatory assassin bug; group housing requires caution because of cannibalism.

Yellow Mealworm Beetle.png.geography_note: Tenebrio molitor is synanthropic and globally introduced through grain storage and husbandry. Its exact native range is uncertain; broad European PA codes should not be treated as confirmed indigenous distribution.

Zebra Longwing.png.geography_note: Heliconius charithonia: native southern Florida and Texas through Mexico, Central America and northern South America. Existing NA/NT OneEarth codes are provisional and should not imply continuous occurrence throughout all assigned polygons.

African Cave Cricket.png.geography_note: Species identification remains unresolved (Phaeophilacris sp. is provisional). The English card name alone cannot justify country or OneEarth assignments. Keep wild_regions empty until identified.
African Cave Cricket.png.taxonomy_note: Card common name does not resolve securely to species; genus-level provisional identification requires verification.
African Cave Cricket.png.taxonomy_audit_note: Species identification unresolved from common name; Phaeophilacris sp. remains provisional. No defensible species-level geographic polygon.
African Cave Cricket.png.taxonomic_note: Phaeophilacris sp. remains provisional. The English card name does not uniquely establish species, so do not assign precise OneEarth regions until the card identification is resolved.

African Olive Millipede.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.

Asian Forest Scorpion.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.
Asian Forest Scorpion.png.taxonomy_audit_note: Heterometrus spinifer is a provisional interpretation of a broad trade/common name; confirm card identification before precise mapping.

Banded Coral Shrimp.png.geography_note: Tropical Indo-Pacific and Atlantic reefs; marine province coverage should reflect warm-water reefs rather than all oceanic waters.
Banded Coral Shrimp.png.habitat_audit_note: Reef crevices and rocky shelter; benthic rather than open-water.
Banded Coral Shrimp.png.population_note: Usually territorial as adults; established male-female pairs are appropriate, but arbitrary multiple adults should not be treated as a colony.
Banded Coral Shrimp.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Blue Death Feigning Beetle.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.
Blue Death Feigning Beetle.png.habitat_audit_note: Desert scrub and sandy/rocky desert of the southwestern United States; do not generalize across all North American deserts.

Brazilian Whiteknee Tarantula.png.geography_note: Known from northern Brazil, notably Pará. Do not extrapolate this to all Amazonian NT regions; OneEarth polygon assignment awaits verified locality-to-region matching. Provisional coarse OneEarth coverage for northern Brazilian Amazon/Pará; exact region boundary intersection still requires map verification.
Brazilian Whiteknee Tarantula.png.habitat_audit_note: Northern Brazilian Amazon rainforest, with species-level locality verification needed for exact NT regions.

Caribbean Hermit Crab.png.geography_note: Coenobita clypeatus occurs on Caribbean islands and adjacent western Atlantic shores. Native distribution must be checked against island/coastal NT codes; marine province codes are inappropriate for this terrestrial adult. Provisional Caribbean coastal/island coverage; mainland versus island precision must be checked against OneEarth polygons. Existing wild_regions are terrestrial bioregion proxies and must not be interpreted as verified MEOW marine ecoregions.
Caribbean Hermit Crab.png.habitat_audit_note: Terrestrial coastal forests and scrub near the sea; not a marine submerged species.
Caribbean Hermit Crab.png.population_note: Terrestrial adult hermit crab; needs humid land substrate and access to both fresh and salt water. Marine access is essential for larval development. Group housing possible with adequate shells and resources.

Common Desert Centipede.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.

Common Octopus.png.geography_note: Octopus vulgaris sensu stricto: northeastern/eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean; many older tropical worldwide records refer to different cryptic species.
Common Octopus.png.taxonomy_note: Octopus vulgaris sensu stricto; many worldwide records previously attributed to this name belong to related species.
Common Octopus.png.habitat_audit_note: Marine benthic habitat: rocky reefs, crevices and seagrass; coastal tag is a coarse approximation.
Common Octopus.png.taxonomy_audit_note: Octopus vulgaris sensu stricto is narrower than historical worldwide usages of the name.
Common Octopus.png.marine_mapping_note: Provisional northeastern Atlantic candidate subset; Mediterranean and African Atlantic coasts not yet mapped. Codes are inferred from existing inventory comparators, not independently verified against MEOW polygon boundaries.

Dahlia Anemone.png.geography_note: Cold-temperate northeastern Atlantic, including British Isles and adjacent European waters; not a tropical anemone.
Dahlia Anemone.png.habitat_audit_note: Rocky coastal habitat including intertidal pools and subtidal sites.
Dahlia Anemone.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): intertidal.
Dahlia Anemone.png.marine_mapping_note: Provisional northeastern Atlantic coastal subset; wider boreal distribution not yet mapped. Codes are inferred from existing inventory comparators, not independently verified against MEOW polygon boundaries.

Fire Shrimp.png.geography_note: Indo-Pacific reef species, typically sheltered in reef crevices; avoid worldwide tropical coverage.
Fire Shrimp.png.habitat_audit_note: Indo-Pacific reef-associated cleaner shrimp, sheltering in crevices.
Fire Shrimp.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Giant Cave Cockroach.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.

Giant Desert Hairy Scorpion.png.geography_note: Hadrurus arizonensis is primarily a Sonoran Desert species of Arizona and northwestern Mexico. Do not restore the broad NA19–NA28 array used for other southwestern desert arthropods. Provisional Sonoran Desert coverage in southwestern USA/northwestern Mexico; excludes blanket coverage of other North American deserts.
Giant Desert Hairy Scorpion.png.habitat_audit_note: Sonoran desert and neighboring arid habitats; avoid a blanket southwestern North American range.

Giant Spiny Stick Insect.png.geography_note: Native to New Guinea and nearby islands; previously assigned eastern Australian OneEarth codes were inherited from an incorrect identification and have been removed pending accurate regional mapping. IM18 is a provisional New Guinea mainland-level OneEarth assignment. Eurycantha calcarata occurs in New Guinea; verify the specific island and local bioregion before treating the full region as occupied.
Giant Spiny Stick Insect.png.taxonomy_note: Giant Spiny Stick Insect is Eurycantha calcarata, distinct from the Level 1 Spiny Leaf Insect (Extatosoma tiaratum).
Giant Spiny Stick Insect.png.habitat_note: Terrestrial, mostly nocturnal stick insect associated with humid tropical forest; shelters near the forest floor, under bark and in vegetation.

Giant Vinegaroon.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.

Glasswing Butterfly.png.geography_note: Provisional broad native-range region candidates; refine against OneEarth region boundaries before treating as fully audited.
Glasswing Butterfly.png.habitat_note: Cloud and humid tropical forest are characteristic; riverine habitat is not a general requirement.

Greenbottle Blue Tarantula.png.geography_note: Chromatopelma cyaneopubescens is restricted to arid scrub of the Paraguaná Peninsula, northwestern Venezuela. A country-wide Venezuela or northern South America polygon would be inaccurate. Provisional northern Venezuelan region assignment for Paraguaná Peninsula; verify precise polygon before treating this as definitive.
Greenbottle Blue Tarantula.png.habitat_audit_note: Arid thorn scrub of the Paraguaná Peninsula, Venezuela; not widespread Venezuelan rainforest.
Greenbottle Blue Tarantula.png.habitat_note: Dry scrub and thorn woodland in northern Venezuela; not a humid rainforest tarantula.

Banded Orange Heliconian.png.geography_note: Provisional tropical Neotropical region candidates based on other butterfly distributions already in this inventory. Exact local occurrence and OneEarth polygon boundaries still require verification.

Blue Baboon Tarantula.png.geography_note: Socotra Island endemic (Yemen), in dry rocky scrub/woodland. No mainland Yemen, Arabian Peninsula, or Horn of Africa OneEarth code is a defensible proxy. Blue Baboon Tarantula.png.habitat_note: Socotra endemic; do not apply mainland African or Arabian ranges by inference.

Delicate Anemone.png.geography_note: Indo-Pacific sandy and rubble-bottom anemone habitats; Heteractis malu is not a generic Atlantic anemone.

Flat Rock Scorpion.png.geography_note: Provisional southern-African OneEarth coverage based on regional analogues in the inventory; Hadogenes troglodytes occupies rocky crevices in parts of southern Africa, not the entire AT10/AT11 regions. Giant Asian Mantis.png.geography_note: South and Southeast Asia; OneEarth region codes require polygon-level verification before assignment.

Giant Owl Butterfly.png.geography_note: Provisional tropical Neotropical region candidates. Species distribution is patchy and does not occupy all habitats within these broad OneEarth regions.

Gooty Sapphire Tarantula.png.geography_note: Restricted eastern Indian dry deciduous forest near the Andhra Pradesh–Telangana region; captive specimens do not establish a broader wild distribution. Arboreal tree-hole specialist. Gooty Sapphire Tarantula.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): woodland. Restricted Andhra Pradesh population; not interchangeable with widespread Indian ornamental tarantulas.

Great Eggfly.png.geography_note: Hypolimnas bolina occurs from South Asia through Southeast Asia and Australasia into Pacific islands. Current IM candidate codes cover only part of its range. Great Mormon.png.geography_note: Provisional mainland Southeast Asian region candidates; other parts of its Asian distribution remain unmapped pending verification.

Great Orange Tip.png.geography_note: Hebomoia glaucippe ranges across parts of South and Southeast Asia, including mainland and island populations. Existing IM codes are candidate regional coverage only. Check western Indian-subcontinent coverage and the precise limits of island populations before extending the mapped range.

Green Sea Urchin.png.geography_note: Cold northern Atlantic and North Pacific waters; temperate and boreal rocky substrates and kelp beds. Not a tropical reef species.
Green Sea Urchin.png.habitat_audit_note: Cold-water rocky coastal and kelp habitats.
Green Sea Urchin.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): kelp-forest.

Harlequin Shrimp.png.geography_note: Reef-associated Indo-Pacific Hymenocera; species limits versus eastern Pacific H. elegans require care. Specialized sea-star predator.

Harlequin Shrimp.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): coral-reef.

Indian Ornamental Tree Spider.png.geography_note: Peninsular Indian deciduous forests; keep separate from the narrow distribution of Poecilotheria metallica. Arboreal spider using tree cavities. Indian Ornamental Tree Spider.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): woodland.

Japanese Spider Crab.png.geography_note: Waters around Japan in the northwestern Pacific, including deeper shelf and slope habitats; not an all-Pacific spider crab.
Japanese Spider Crab.png.habitat_audit_note: Continental shelf and slope benthic habitats; coastal tag alone is insufficient.
Japanese Spider Crab.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): sandy-seafloor.

Migratory Locust.png.geography_note: Broad Old World distribution with patchy suitable grassland and wetland habitats. Outbreak movements do not justify painting every intervening OneEarth region.

Plain Tiger Butterfly.png.geography_note: Danaus chrysippus has a broad native Afro-Asian range, including many African savannas and dry open habitats, the Indian subcontinent and parts of western/southern Asia. Existing IM2–IM8 codes are provisional and partial; African AT codes cannot be inferred reliably from country labels alone. Do not treat the current mapped regions as its complete range.

Plumose Anemone.png.geography_note: Temperate and cold northern coastal waters, attached to hard substrate; do not map as tropical reef species.

Plumose Anemone.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): intertidal.

Rainbow Stag Beetle.png.geography_note: Phalacrognathus muelleri is native to rainforest areas of northeastern Queensland and New Guinea. Red Lacewing Butterfly.png.geography_note: Provisional mainland Southeast Asian region candidates; this is partial coverage only, not a verified full native-range map.

Scarlet Mormon.png.geography_note: Philippines and Taiwan; do not infer occurrence on mainland Southeast Asia from the broader Papilio memnon complex. Sexy Shrimp.png.geography_note: Anemone-associated tropical marine shrimp; Thor amboinensis identification may encompass geographically structured cryptic lineages.

Red-Legged Fire Millipede.png.habitat_note: Specific habitat descriptors (not currently in canonical game tag vocabulary): forest-floor.

Simandoa Cave Roach.png.geography_note: Known from Guinea cave locality; extinct in the wild, maintained in captivity. Do not assign an entire West African region to a single documented Guinean cave locality; retain unmapped pending polygon verification.
