Winters primarily in India and northeastern Africa. The wild_regions codes are a provisional broad seasonal distribution, not a verified breeding-only map; migration transit should not by itself justify a region.
Demoiselle Crane.png.migration_note: Migratory; native seasonal breeding and wintering distributions are distinct. Region-code array does not currently encode season.

Emu.png.geography_note: Native across most of mainland Australia; Tasmania population is extinct and all non-Australian Australasian regions removed.
Emu.png.population_note: Breeding pairs are the default adult social unit; managed groups can occur with careful introduction and ample space.

Greater Rhea.png.population_note: Polygynous breeding groups with extensive paddock space; males may become territorial in the breeding season.

Grey Crowned Crane.png.geography_note: Eastern and southern African wetland-grassland crane: eastern DRC/Uganda/Kenya south through Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique, plus Zimbabwe/South Africa and small populations west to Angola/Namibia.
Grey Crowned Crane.png.population_note: Adult cranes are primarily maintained as territorial breeding pairs; family groups with dependent offspring are temporary, not routine stable multi-pair breeding groups. Allow larger nonbreeding flocks only with suitable management.

Red-Crowned Crane.png.population_note: Adult cranes are primarily maintained as territorial breeding pairs; family groups with dependent offspring are temporary, not routine stable multi-pair breeding groups. Allow larger nonbreeding flocks only with suitable management.
Red-Crowned Crane.png.geography_note: Breeds in northeast Asia, especially Amur/Ussuri basin and northeast China, with resident population in Hokkaido; winters in Korea and eastern China. Removed western Siberian and Tibetan regions. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Blue Eared Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native to high-elevation mountains of central/western China, especially Qinghai, Gansu, Sichuan and Ningxia, on the northeastern Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Field research at Wanglang (Sichuan) documents use of high-elevation shrub habitats. PA42–PA45 remains a provisional coarse regional assignment, not a confirmed polygon-level range. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.
Blue Eared Pheasant.png.population_note: Occurs in groups outside breeding season; breeding pairs and small managed groups are reasonable abstractions.

California Quail.png.geography_note: Native chiefly to the western United States and Baja California/northwestern Mexico; excludes eastern Great Plains and Great Lakes. Introduced populations outside native range omitted. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Common Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native populations span the Caucasus/Caspian region, Central Asia, eastern Siberia, mainland China and Taiwan (represented by IM13). Most European, North American and Australasian populations are introduced and excluded. The large PA-region range is an approximate footprint of fragmented native subspecies distributions, not continuous occupancy. Sources: Scientific Reports (2021), doi:10.1038/s41598-021-00567-1; birdfinding.info/common-pheasant/.

Crested Partridge.png.geography_note: Native to lowland rainforests of the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Borneo, with Java also reported; removed Indian, Himalayan and northern Indochinese regions. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Domestic Turkey.png.geography_note: Domestic form; no native wild distribution assigned. Do not copy the wild turkey range.

Edwards's Pheasant.png.geography_note: Historical native range restricted to lowland evergreen forest in central Viet Nam: Ha Tinh, Quang Binh, Quang Tri and Thua Thien Hue. Possibly extinct in the wild; last confirmed wild record in 2000. IM5 is provisional pending OneEarth boundary verification; no Laos extension. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.
Edwards's Pheasant.png.population_note: Pair or carefully managed breeding group; species should not be treated as a widespread dry-forest pheasant.

Eurasian Crane.png.population_note: Adult cranes are primarily maintained as territorial breeding pairs; family groups with dependent offspring are temporary, not routine stable multi-pair breeding groups. Allow larger nonbreeding flocks only with suitable management.
Eurasian Crane.png.geography_note: Breeds across northern and western Europe, Russia and Siberia to northern Mongolia and northern China. Winters in western/southern Europe, northern and eastern Africa, the Middle East, India and southern/eastern China. Existing wild_regions are a provisional broad distribution and have not been validated against the exact OneEarth polygons; breeding, wintering and transit occurrences should be distinguished.
Eurasian Crane.png.migration_note: Migratory; native seasonal breeding and wintering distributions are distinct. Region-code array does not currently encode season.

Eurasian Quail.png.geography_note: Common Quail (Coturnix coturnix) breeds across Europe and western/central Asia and has wintering populations in Africa and southern Asia. Easternmost PA43–PA45 removed as an overly broad extension toward eastern Asia, where Japanese Quail (Coturnix japonica) is a distinct species. Remaining region codes are coarse year-round approximations and need boundary-level validation; migration corridors are not equivalent to continuous occupancy. Sources: IUCN 2018 species assessment; Animal Diversity Web geographic account; eBird seasonal range mapping.

Golden Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native to montane forests of central China; introduced populations elsewhere (including Britain) must not count toward wild_regions. Current PA codes provisional until region boundary verification. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.

Grey Peacock-Pheasant.png.geography_note: Mainland Southeast Asian forest species, from northeastern India/Myanmar into Indochina and southern China; removed western Indian regions. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Himalayan Monal.png.geography_note: Himalayan mountain forests and alpine scrub from Afghanistan/Pakistan through Nepal/Bhutan into Tibet; removed Central Asian deserts and Kazakh steppe regions. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Indian Peafowl.png.geography_note: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Sri Lanka, primarily dry/open woodland and forest edge; introduced populations omitted. OneEarth bioregion approximations, not precise occurrence polygons.

Lady Amherst's Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native to southwest China and adjacent northern Myanmar; introduced populations in Britain and elsewhere excluded. Current broad PA/IM region codes need polygon-level verification. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.

Reeves's Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native to fragmented forest landscapes of central China, especially Henan, Hubei, Anhui and Guizhou; historical records also extend into adjoining provinces. Recent studies locate key habitats in Henan, Hubei, Anhui and Guizhou. Introduced European populations excluded. PA42–PA45 requires polygon verification before any pruning. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.

Silky Chicken.png.geography_note: Domestic chicken breed; no native wild distribution assigned. Do not copy the red junglefowl range.

Silver Pheasant.png.geography_note: Native to forested mainland Southeast Asia and southern China, including Viet Nam, Laos, Myanmar and Thailand; do not treat every southern Chinese or Indomalayan bioregion as occupied.

Swinhoe's Pheasant.png.geography_note: Endemic resident of Taiwan, especially forested hills and mountains. One Earth assigns Taiwan Subtropical Evergreen Forests and South Taiwan Monsoon Rainforests to South China Subtropical Evergreen & Monsoon Forests (IM13). IM13 is a broad bioregion also covering mainland areas; Taiwan-only occupancy cannot be distinguished by this bioregion code alone.

Temminck's Tragopan.png.geography_note: Native mountain-forest distribution from northeastern India and northern Myanmar through south-central China to northern Viet Nam; concentrated in southern/central China, not throughout East Asia. PA and IM codes provisional pending finer OneEarth matching. OneEarth region assignment revised in pass 6; region coverage is approximate and includes only native distribution, with boundary overlap needing map-level verification.

Black Crowned Crane.png.geography_note: West African/Sahel-Sudanian crane of shallow wetlands and grasslands from Senegal east toward Sudan/Ethiopia; oceanic islands and southern-African blanket codes excluded.

Blue Crane.png.geography_note: Southern African grassland crane concentrated in South Africa, with marginal occurrence in Namibia/Botswana. Old Sahel/Horn-style array removed.

Common Ostrich.png.geography_note: Native African ostrich distribution across Sahel/Horn/East African and southern African open drylands, with Saharan margins retained. Oceanic islands, humid Congo/West African forest cores and extinct/introduced-only areas excluded.

Southern Ground Hornbill.png.geography_note: Savanna/woodland bird from Kenya/Tanzania south through Angola/Zambia/Zimbabwe/Mozambique/Botswana into northeastern South Africa. Similar to Plains Zebra geographically but not identical; Horn-of-Africa extension removed.

Southern Cassowary.png.geography_note: Native to New Guinea, adjacent Aru/Seram-area islands and northeastern Queensland; corrected erroneous NZ/Lord Howe/Indomalayan codes.

Wattled Crane.png.geography_note: Three principal populations: south-central Africa (especially Zambia/Botswana/Angola/DRC/Tanzania/Zimbabwe), isolated Ethiopian population, and eastern South Africa. Similarity to Grey Crowned Crane is genuine at OneEarth resolution.

Kori Bustard.png.geography_note: Open-country bustard with eastern and southern African populations. Existing broad savanna/dryland range confirmed.

Laughing Kookaburra.png.geography_note: Native eastern Australia; western Australian and New Zealand populations are introduced and excluded.

Galah.png.geography_note: Native across mainland Australia and Tasmania; removed all non-Australian Australasian island regions.

Nicobar Pigeon.png.geography_note: Native to small offshore islands from the Andaman–Nicobar archipelago through parts of island Southeast Asia, New Guinea and the western Pacific. IM15, IM18 and AU12 are partial island-region proxies (Philippines, New Guinea and Solomon Islands); the Nicobar/Andaman core and other islands still need polygon-level verification. Do not interpret these broad regions as full mainland occupancy.

Green Turaco.png.geography_note: Primarily West African forest turaco under the current card concept, concentrated from Senegambia/Guinea east through the Upper Guinea and western Lower Guinea forests. Congo/East/southern African template regions removed.

Kea.png.geography_note: Endemic to New Zealand's South Island; corrected AU16 Subantarctic Antipodes Islands.

Little Corella.png.geography_note: Native Australian range only; removed New Zealand, Pacific, New Guinea, Sulawesi and other island spillover.

Livingstone's Turaco.png.geography_note: Southeastern African forest turaco from Tanzania/Malawi through Mozambique and eastern Zimbabwe to northeastern South Africa. Existing range confirmed.

Pink Cockatoo.png.geography_note: Arid and semi-arid inland Australia; removed New Guinea and surrounding Australasian/Pacific islands.

Purple-Crested Turaco.png.geography_note: Southeastern African woodland/forest turaco; slightly broader westward/south-central reach than Livingstone's Turaco. Duplicate equality removed.

Silvery-Cheeked Hornbill.png.geography_note: Montane and coastal forest hornbill of Ethiopia and East Africa south through Tanzania to Malawi/Mozambique. Southern highveld region inherited through the Mountain Reedbuck match removed.

Timneh Parrot.png.geography_note: Upper Guinea endemic from Guinea-Bissau/Guinea through Sierra Leone and Liberia to western Côte d'Ivoire, with only marginal southern Mali occurrence; old oceanic-island and East/Southern African codes removed.

Trumpeter Hornbill.png.geography_note: Resident eastern/south-central African forest hornbill: DRC/Burundi/Kenya/Tanzania through Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe to Botswana, Namibia's Caprivi and eastern South Africa. West African, Horn dryland and oceanic-island codes excluded.

Blue-Winged Kookaburra.png.geography_note: Northern Australia and southern New Guinea; corrected NZ/Lord Howe/eastern-temperate and Indomalayan assignments.

Tawny Frogmouth.png.geography_note: Native throughout Australia including Tasmania; removed New Zealand, Pacific islands, New Guinea, Sulawesi and subantarctic codes.

African Grey Hornbill.png.geography_note: Widespread African woodland/savanna hornbill from West Africa and the Sahel through Central/East Africa into southern Africa. Added missing western/central forest-edge region AT15 rather than retaining the warthog-identical template.

Bearded Barbet.png.geography_note: West African resident of wooded Sahel and savanna from Senegambia/Guinea-Bissau east through southern Chad and south to Guinea, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Benin, Nigeria, Cameroon and northwestern CAR. Old oceanic-island and southern-African assignments removed.

Long-Billed Corella.png.geography_note: Native southeastern Australia; removed Solomon, New Guinea, Sulawesi and southeast Indonesian island codes.

Meyer's Parrot.png.geography_note: Species-level range combining all Meyer's Parrot subspecies: southern Chad/northeastern Cameroon east to Eritrea and western Ethiopia, then south through Uganda/Kenya/Tanzania and south-central Africa to Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique and northern South Africa.

Palm Cockatoo.png.geography_note: Cape York Peninsula and New Guinea/Aru region; corrected erroneous NZ/Lord Howe/Indomalayan assignments.

Red-Billed Hornbill.png.geography_note: Red-billed Hornbill complex mapped at the current card's species-level concept: Sahel/Sudanian dry country east to Somalia/northern Tanzania plus southern populations from Angola through Botswana/Namibia/Zimbabwe to northern South Africa; humid West/Central forest cores excluded.

Red-Tailed Black Cockatoo.png.geography_note: Australian mainland distribution; removed New Zealand, Pacific, New Guinea and Indonesian island spillover.

White-Crested Turaco.png.geography_note: Riverine forest and woodland species in a belt from eastern Nigeria/Cameroon across Central Africa to western Kenya. Southern and far-western regions inherited from the duplicate template removed.

Black-Casqued Hornbill.png.geography_note: West/Central African lowland rainforest hornbill from Upper Guinea east through Cameroon/Gabon/Congo into the Congo basin; old East/southern-African-style duplicate array removed.

Crowned Hornbill.png.geography_note: Eastern and southern African wooded-habitat hornbill from southern Ethiopia/Somalia through East Africa to South Africa, extending west through DRC to Angola. Oceanic islands and West African forest/Sahel overreach excluded.

Grey-Cheeked Hornbill.png.geography_note: Central/East African rainforest hornbill from Cameroon/CAR through Congo/DRC to Uganda and western Kenya/Tanzania, with Albertine Rift occurrence; old duplicate array corrected.

Red-Billed Woodhoopoe.png.geography_note: Broad mainland sub-Saharan woodland species from West Africa through the Sahel and East Africa to southern Africa. Somalia is primarily vagrant/non-breeding; oceanic islands and deep rainforest-core blanket assignments excluded.

Schalow's Turaco.png.geography_note: South-central/eastern African montane-forest turaco centered on the Albertine Rift and adjacent highlands, extending through Zambia/Angola into Malawi/Tanzania. Oceanic-island code AT18 and West African forest assignments removed.

Gang-Gang Cockatoo.png.geography_note: Southeastern Australia; removed western Australia, New Guinea, Sulawesi and southeast Indonesian island codes.

Great Blue Turaco.png.geography_note: West/Central African forest turaco extending east into the Great Lakes/Albertine region; old identical range shared with unrelated taxa replaced.

Knobbed Hornbill.png.geography_note: Sulawesi endemic also occurring on nearby Lembeh, Togian, Muna and Buton/Butung; corrected IM14 (Nansei Islands) to AU14 Sulawesi & Maluku Islands.

Northern Kaka.png.geography_note: North Island New Zealand taxon; corrected OC1 Easter Island to AU1 New Zealand.

Yellow-Tailed Black Cockatoo.png.geography_note: Southeastern and southern Australia including Tasmania; removed New Guinea, Solomon, Sulawesi, southeast Indonesian and subantarctic codes.

African Sacred Ibis.png.geography_note: Extremely widespread native African wetland bird including Madagascar, plus native Middle-Eastern populations in Iraq/Iran and Yemen. Introduced European populations excluded.

African Spoonbill.png.geography_note: Widespread African wetland spoonbill from sub-Saharan mainland to Madagascar. Madagascar is native and deliberately retained; unrelated oceanic-island systems are excluded.

Great White Pelican.png.geography_note: Very wide Old World pelican with African breeding/non-breeding populations plus southeastern Europe, western/central Asia and South Asia. False African oceanic-island and Congo-forest blanket codes removed.

Greater Flamingo.png.geography_note: Highly mobile saline-wetland species; broad Africa–Mediterranean–Asia range remains appropriate and is not reduced merely to break a duplicate.

Abdim's Stork.png.geography_note: Intra-African migrant breeding across the Sahel from Senegal to Ethiopia/Somalia and moving through East Africa to southern Africa in the non-breeding season. Regular seasonal range is included.

Glossy Ibis.png.geography_note: Cosmopolitan wetland bird. Regular native/breeding range spans southern/eastern Europe, Africa including Madagascar, central/southern Asia, Southeast Asia, New Guinea and Australia; vagrant-only northern European occurrence excluded.

Hamerkop.png.geography_note: Widespread African wetland bird; Madagascar included. Broad continental occurrence is legitimate rather than a savanna-template artifact.

Marabou Stork.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan scavenging/wetland stork. Central African occurrence retained and AT15 added; broad mobility means substantial overlap with savanna mammals is real, but the exact inherited array was too restrictive.

Yellow-Billed Stork.png.geography_note: Extremely widespread resident/nomadic African wetland stork including Madagascar. Middle-Eastern and European records are vagrancy only and are excluded.

Pink-Backed Pelican.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan freshwater and coastal pelican from West/Central Africa through East Africa to southern Africa. False oceanic-island codes AT3/AT4/AT5/AT18 removed.

Allen's Gallinule.png.geography_note: Sub-Saharan wetland species with broad tropical African occurrence and seasonal movements; oceanic islands and driest southwest/Horn regions excluded.

Black Crake.png.geography_note: Very widespread resident African wetland rail. Broad mainland range is legitimate, but its geography is separated from unrelated Egyptian Fruit Bat and Nile Crocodile template matches.

Hadada Ibis.png.geography_note: Sub-Saharan wetland/grassland ibis from West/Central Africa through East Africa to southern Africa; dry Horn/Sahel fringe trimmed relative to the inherited broad template.

Saddle-Billed Stork.png.geography_note: Patchy sub-Saharan wetland species: southern Sahel/West Africa and more continuous Nile/East/south-central African occurrence to northern Botswana, Mozambique and eastern South Africa.

Straw-Necked Ibis.png.geography_note: Australia and Tasmania; removed New Guinea, Sulawesi, Solomon, Vanuatu and other island spillover.

Lesser Flamingo.png.geography_note: Highly mobile African flamingo concentrated at alkaline lakes and pans in East and southern Africa, with West African/Sahel and South Asian populations. False AT18 island assignment and humid forest blanket regions removed.

African Openbill.png.geography_note: Widespread sub-Saharan wetland stork with native Madagascar occurrence. Broad river, marsh and floodplain distribution retained; extreme arid regions excluded.

Little Grebe.png.geography_note: Very widespread freshwater grebe across Europe, much of Asia, Southeast Asia/west Pacific, New Guinea and most of Africa including Madagascar. Arid interiors without suitable wetlands remain ecological gaps within broad regions.

Brolga.png.geography_note: Northern and eastern mainland Australia with inland occurrences; all New Zealand/Pacific/New Guinea/Sulawesi codes removed.

Green Sea Turtle.png.geography_audit_note: Deferred to marine-range audit: oceanic/marine distribution should not be approximated by blanket terrestrial Australasian bioregions.

Rockhopper Penguin.png.geography_note: Oceanic-island range is intentional for this species; AT3 is not removed merely because it is a diagnostic error code on mainland taxa. Retained pending/subject to island-level species-complex mapping.

Baltic Seal.png.taxonomy_note: Asset is named Baltic Seal, but scientific_name is species-level Pusa hispida; Nearctic mapping follows the full species (Ringed Seal), not only Baltic subspecies P. h. botnica.

Green Sawfish.png.geography_note: Madagascar coastal occurrence is historically plausible but current presence of Pristis zijsron is unconfirmed (2026 review); MEOW-E099/E100 excluded pending verified extant records.

notes.geography: Animal geography is stored in wild_regions (One Earth), marine_regions (MEOW), and pelagic_regions (PPOW), not duplicated as continent/subregion tags.
notes.composition: Habitat tags are compositional: for example, swamp forest is represented by a forest tag plus wetland rather than a separate swamp tag.
notes.categoryAndLevel: Category and rarity level remain encoded by the Category -> Level hierarchy.

zooTypeWeights.typeSelectionRule: Zoo type comes from the grouped zoo-name prefix database; unrecognized/custom names default to general unless the player explicitly selects a type.

general.description: No collection bias; baseline weighting for a general zoological collection.

aquarium.description: Aquatic specialist. Strongly favours aquatic animals; also mildly favours wetland, semi-aquatic and tropical species, with a small reptile overlap from aquatic/terrarium husbandry.

tropical.description: Climate-controlled tropical collection. Favours rainforest species, with natural secondary overlap into reptiles, small mammals and tropical aquatic/semi-aquatic exhibits.

safari.description: Large open-range collection. Favours African savanna ungulates most strongly, with weaker preferences for associated carnivores, large birds and dry-country species.

forest.description: Woodland collection. Favours temperate/boreal forest fauna, with smaller biases toward woodland carnivores, ungulates and forest-wetland species.

farm.description: Domestic and contact-animal collection. Domestic status dominates; ungulates and familiar temperate mammals receive only small secondary preferences.

bird.description: Bird specialist with aviaries and climate-controlled houses. Strongly favours all bird categories, with modest wetland/tropical overlap and only a very small reptile-house crossover.

reptile.description: Mostly indoor terrarium specialist. Strongly favours reptiles, but its heated indoor exhibits and aquarium/terrarium expertise also make tropical, aquatic, semi-aquatic, desert and nocturnal species more likely.

alpine.description: Mountain collection. Strongly favours mountain fauna, with smaller cold-climate and mountain-associated ungulate, carnivore and raptor preferences.

raptor.description: Raptor and falconry specialist. Very strongly favours Birds of Prey while retaining a small chance of other bird groups and habitat-associated species.

butterfly.description: Four distinct Level 1 butterflies at startup; remaining starting species come from other categories with a strong tropical/rainforest bias.

insectarium.description: Invertebrate-focused zoo, with two or three non-invertebrate starting species prioritising freshwater and birds.

incomingTradeOffers.rule: For each category/tag multiplier M above, use 1 + ((M - 1) * tradePreferenceStrength). This preserves the same preference direction but makes incoming offers less type-dominated than starting generation.

notes: Category and tag bonuses stack multiplicatively, then are capped.
No type excludes animals: a non-matching animal retains baseline weight 1.0.
Level/rarity is deliberately not part of zoo-type weighting; existing game progression rules continue to control levels.
Continent tags are currently used directly only by safari (Africa). They remain available for later regional/specialist zoo types.
Nocturnal is retained as animal metadata for a future nocturnal-house or nocturnal-zoo preference; it is not forced into an unrelated current type.

Logic pass v2 adds restrained secondary preferences based on likely facilities and husbandry expertise (e.g. reptile zoos also favour tropical and aquatic animals). Primary identity bonuses remain substantially stronger than crossover bonuses.
